AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA V
Dr. Sora Kel
Everyone keeps asking whether PT-9 can damage a reactor vessel. Wrong question. The vessel is not the vulnerability.

Look around: cable insulation, coolant seals, pump gaskets, control wiring, sensor housings, protective membranes, emergency batteries. A reactor does not need its core destroyed to stop being useful.
It needs one sufficiently important auxiliary system to fail. Helion can replace components. For now. But maintenance inventory is being consumed faster than manufacturing replaces it.
The power system isn't collapsing because generators forgot how to generate. It's collapsing because civilization is made out of interfaces. And interfaces are everywhere.

AUDIO TRANSCRIPT
ERA VII
Helion Control Engineer
Central Grid Authority is gone. No response for six hours. We're separating from the eastern network. Karsic strike warnings triggered three times this morning. Nobody knows whether they're real.

Unit Two is stable. Unit Three is shutting down. We have enough fuel. Fuel isn't the problem. We don't have replacement coolant seals. We don't have staff. Half the transmission substations are offline.
This plant can generate enough power for a million homes while half those homes remain dark because there is no intact system between us and them.
That's the story of the whole damn world now. Plenty of capability. No system left to carry it.
